texture/av_rock05_c.dds@da173111.description: Dark grey-brown mottled rock with rusty stains.
texture/av_rock05_c.dds@da173111.usage: Wall of Slaughter's rock models at about 34 units per repeat with av_rock05_n: weathered boulders and outcrops, not warm canyon walls.

texture/av_rock05_n.dds@b0d60d3a.usage: The normal texture of a material whose diffuse is av_rock05_c.dds; at the same repeat.

texture/blend_sand_rock.dds@304ec155.description: Ochre rock with a thin fringe of pale sand along its lower edge; repeats across.
texture/blend_sand_rock.dds@304ec155.usage: Like blend_sand_rock_lg with a narrower sand fringe, for a rock base meeting sand on gentler ground; not placed in Sunderock's geometry. Pairs with blend_sand_rock_5n.

texture/blend_sand_rock_5n.dds@7f7b8d01.usage: The normal texture of a material whose diffuse is blend_sand_rock.dds; at the same repeat.

texture/blend_sand_rock_lg.dds@bbf9255e.description: Ochre rock over its upper two thirds fading through a ragged edge into a broad band of pale sand along the bottom; repeats across but not down.
texture/blend_sand_rock_lg.dds@bbf9255e.usage: The foot of a rock face where it meets sand: map it once vertically with the sand band at the ground line and repeat it along the wall (it tiles horizontally only); Sunderock's spires use about 20 units per repeat, and big cliffs can go to 40. Pairs with blend_sand_rock_lg10n; the rock above takes rock_light2 or rock_light5 and the ground di_tak_ruin_sand2.

texture/blend_sand_rock_lg10n.dds@de686f.usage: The normal texture of a material whose diffuse is blend_sand_rock_lg.dds; at the same repeat.

texture/canwall1.bmp@acc2b333.description: Classic-era dark ochre canyon wall with eroded ridges and deep shadows.
texture/canwall1.bmp@acc2b333.usage: Oasis of Marr's canyon walls at about 130 units per repeat on steep slopes; softer and darker than the Underfoot rocks, for distant or shaded walls.

texture/cavefloordrk2_c.dds@923c5e4f.description: Plain dark brown fine earth, nearly uniform.
texture/cavefloordrk2_c.dds@923c5e4f.usage: Cave floors and shaded ground: Goru'kar Mesa's grass-dirt recipe at about 10 units per repeat.

texture/cavewall.dds@568482fc.description: The same rose-red sandstone as cavewall2 with its marks running vertically: runnels and cracks top to bottom.
texture/cavewall.dds@568482fc.usage: Vertical companion to cavewall2 for cave roofs and walls where the grain should run down; the Scarlet Desert used it mostly on overhangs at about 55 units per repeat.

texture/cavewall2.dds@ca260dbb.description: Dusty rose-red sandstone with horizontal ledges, pits, and crumbling bands; soft, low contrast detail.
texture/cavewall2.dds@ca260dbb.usage: Red canyon and cave walls: the Scarlet Desert covers its walls and cave roofs with it at about 78 units per repeat. Its horizontal ledges suit layered canyon strata; box-project on walls and keep the repeat large, as it goes soft up close.

texture/deposits_pools.dds@dabe929d.description: Pale yellow and white mineral crust in blotchy layers, like the rim of a hot spring.
texture/deposits_pools.dds@dabe929d.usage: Rims and terraces of mineral pools on gentle slopes (Sunderock's pools recipe, slopes 8 to 23 degrees, about 13 units per repeat); bright enough to need small areas.

texture/di_lolands_river_bottom.dds@d017.description: Grey-tan pebbles and shell-like fragments packed tightly, like a dry stream bed.
texture/di_lolands_river_bottom.dds@d017.usage: River and pool beds under the water line: Sunderock's river recipes apply it at the river's heights on slopes up to 45 degrees, about 13 units per repeat, with di_lolands_river_bottom_4n.

texture/di_lolands_river_bottom_4n.dds@4.usage: The normal texture of a material whose diffuse is di_lolands_river_bottom.dds; at the same repeat.

texture/di_lolands_sulfur_ground.dds@eac.description: Yellow-green sulfur crust mottled over pale ground.
texture/di_lolands_sulfur_ground.dds@eac.usage: Flats around sulfur vents: Sunderock's sulfur recipe on slopes of 8 to 45 degrees within a band of heights, about 13 units per repeat, with di_lolands_sulfur_ground_12n.

texture/di_lolands_sulfur_ground_12n.dds.usage: The normal texture of a material whose diffuse is di_lolands_sulfur_ground.dds; at the same repeat.

texture/di_ro_sand_grass2.dds@2cae8bf1.description: Sparse green grass tufts over tan sand, about half and half.
texture/di_ro_sand_grass2.dds@2cae8bf1.usage: Grass where sand gets water: oases, riverbanks, sheltered canyon floors. Sunderock uses it at about 13 units per repeat with di_ro_sand_grass2n; a natural step between di_tak_ruin_sand2 and full grass.

texture/di_ro_sand_grass2n.dds@a2a6548f.usage: The normal texture of a material whose diffuse is di_ro_sand_grass2.dds; at the same repeat.

texture/di_tak__ruin_grnd2_plain.dds@381.description: Brown packed earth with faint mottling; plain trodden ground.
texture/di_tak__ruin_grnd2_plain.dds@381.usage: Trails and bare ground: Goru'kar Mesa's paths recipe at about 13 units per repeat and its barren ground at about 10, with di_tak__ruin_grnd_plain_n.

texture/di_tak__ruin_grnd_plain_n.dds@c4.usage: The normal texture of a material whose diffuse is di_tak__ruin_grnd2_plain.dds; at the same repeat.

texture/di_tak_ruin_sand2.dds@a4789fca.description: Pale cream fine sand with faint soft ripples; almost featureless.
texture/di_tak_ruin_sand2.dds@a4789fca.usage: Sandy flats, canyon floors, and paths: Sunderock's ground recipes lay it on all ground at about 43 units per repeat with di_tak_ruin_sand_6n. Plain enough to need breaking up: rock_light2 on slopes, river rocks in beds, grassy sand by water.

texture/di_tak_ruin_sand_6n.dds@7f48fdc9.usage: The normal texture of a material whose diffuse is di_tak_ruin_sand2.dds; at the same repeat.

texture/dirtwall.dds@605d3ce4.description: Warm orange-tan layered rock with blocky ledges, crisp cracks, and pale weathered faces; reads as canyon sandstone.
texture/dirtwall.dds@605d3ce4.usage: Barren Coast's tower uses it at about 16 units per repeat with dirtwall_n3. A crisp warm canyon rock: cliffs at 40 to 60 units per repeat with box projection, and carved rock dwellings at closer repeats. Alternate with dirtwallb on long walls.

texture/dirtwall_n3.dds@c60e6fab.usage: The normal texture of a material whose diffuse is dirtwall.dds; at the same repeat.

texture/dirtwallb.dds@2686115b.description: A variant of dirtwall: the same warm layered orange-tan rock with its ledges and cracks in other places.
texture/dirtwallb.dds@2686115b.usage: Alternate with dirtwall to break repetition on large walls; Sunderock uses it on small forge props at about 6 units per repeat with dirtwall_n3.

texture/greytranswl.dds@b1eef270.description: Dark speckled grey rock above, giving way to the rose-red sandstone of cavewall2 below; repeats across, not down.
texture/greytranswl.dds@b1eef270.usage: Where dark rock meets red sandstone on a wall: map it once vertically and repeat it along the wall; the Scarlet Desert uses it at about 56 units per repeat.

texture/kl_sand_6n.dds@e2b7c70d.usage: The normal texture of a material whose diffuse is kl_sand_dirt_dead.dds; at the same repeat.

texture/kl_sand_dirt_dead.dds@8c76cb89.description: Brown dirt patched with pale dead grass.
texture/kl_sand_dirt_dead.dds@8c76cb89.usage: Dry ground with dead grass between sand and grass: Goru'kar Mesa's dry ground at about 10 units per repeat with kl_sand_6n.

texture/kl_sand_grey_dead.dds@b3065cb4.description: Grey ashy sand with paler blotches.
texture/kl_sand_grey_dead.dds@b3065cb4.usage: Grey dead ground in hollows and lairs: Goru'kar Mesa's harpy hole on slopes under 30 degrees.

texture/lolands_sulfur_rock01.dds@be0d11.description: Brown rock crusted with bright orange and yellow sulfur or lichen blooms.
texture/lolands_sulfur_rock01.dds@be0d11.usage: Accent rock for sulfur springs and mineral vents (Sunderock's sulfur spires, about 37 units per repeat, with lolands_sulfur_rock01_6n); too loud for broad walls.

texture/lolands_sulfur_rock01_6n.dds@b16.usage: The normal texture of a material whose diffuse is lolands_sulfur_rock01.dds; at the same repeat.

texture/newwat1.dds@f3bc6474.description: Deep blue water flecked with white sparkles.
texture/newwat1.dds@f3bc6474.usage: A classic open-water surface (Hollowshade, Dawnshroud, the Scarlet Desert) at 26 to 116 units per repeat; too dark and blue for a turquoise canyon river.

texture/ngrass4_c.dds@00e839aa.description: Lush, dense green grass blades with a slight diagonal grain.
texture/ngrass4_c.dds@00e839aa.usage: Green meadow ground: Goru'kar Mesa's main ground at about 19 units per repeat. Too lush for a dry canyon except watered terraces and gardens.

texture/riverrocks2.dds@7a77a868.description: Rounded river stones in browns, tans, and greys, packed shoulder to shoulder with dark gaps.
texture/riverrocks2.dds@7a77a868.usage: River beds, streambanks, stony shores, and dry washes: Goru'kar Mesa uses it below the water line at about 19 units per repeat with riverrocks_n. Reads well at the waterline beside sand.

texture/riverrocks_n.dds@97b9368b.usage: The normal texture of a material whose diffuse is riverrocks2.dds; at the same repeat.

texture/rock_light2.dds@d0386cbb.description: Pale tan sandstone with the same crumpled, streaked surface as rock_light5, a little lighter and less yellow.
texture/rock_light2.dds@d0386cbb.usage: Terrain slopes steeper than about 40 degrees, as Sunderock's ground recipes apply it, at about 43 units per repeat with rock_light_10n. A near twin of rock_light5, so the two alternate on long walls to hide repetition.

texture/rock_light5.dds@f972d95c.description: Ochre-yellow sandstone face with a crumpled, wind-carved surface and faint horizontal streaks; reads as warm, dry rock from a distance.
texture/rock_light5.dds@f972d95c.usage: Steep and vertical canyon walls and large rock models: Sunderock covers its cliffs with it at about 49 units per repeat. Box-project on cliffs and pair with rock_light_10n. Yellow rather than red; blends down into rock_light2 and blend_sand_rock_lg at the foot of a wall.

texture/rock_light_10n.dds@f61a9afb.usage: The normal texture of a material whose diffuse is rock_light2.dds; at the same repeat.

texture/rockface2_c.dds@de1bae1e.description: Dark earthy brown rock, finely mottled with faint cracks and darker stains; low contrast.
texture/rockface2_c.dds@de1bae1e.usage: Goru'kar Mesa's recipes put it on slopes over 25 to 30 degrees at about 38 units per repeat with rockface_n. A dark, earthy cliff for shaded walls, cave mouths, and overhang undersides rather than sunlit red rock.

texture/rockface_n.dds@4efffe63.usage: The normal texture of a material whose diffuse is rockface2_c.dds; at the same repeat.

texture/sp_ft_wall_mid.dds@06a766dc.description: Courses of dark stained stone blocks with rust-red streaks and pale mortar.
texture/sp_ft_wall_mid.dds@06a766dc.usage: Built fortress walls: Wall of Slaughter's fortress at about 48 units per repeat, with di_ent_cinderblock01_mid_n.

texture/twicliff01.dds@7807df97.description: Red striped cliff rock at only 64 by 64 pixels; banded but blurry.
texture/twicliff01.dds@7807df97.usage: The Scarlet Desert's giant cliff walls at about 180 units per repeat. It blurs badly at eye height; only for distant backdrop cliffs.

texture/wtr_waterfall_tileb.dds@c3790289.description: Frothing white water with pale teal under the foam, streaked top to bottom, edges fraying into transparency.
texture/wtr_waterfall_tileb.dds@c3790289.usage: Heavy white falls, cascades, and geysers (Sunderock's geyser, about 130 units per repeat); the base of a fall that uses wtr_waterfall_tilec above.

texture/wtr_waterfall_tilec.dds@970059de.description: Falling water: teal sheets streaked with white foam running top to bottom, its side edges fraying into transparency.
texture/wtr_waterfall_tilec.dds@970059de.usage: Waterfall faces: map it so the streaks fall down the face; Sunderock's waterfall models stretch it about 190 units per repeat. The frayed alpha suits falling water, not pools; pair with wtr_waterfall_tileb where the fall whitens.
